EXPORT INSPECTIONS @ 10 AM, CROP PROGRESS @ 3 PM
MARKET HEADLINES
• Quick Editorial: corn led solid trade volume overnight, with the key CZ and
SX contracts posting fresh move highs early last night before ratcheting back
into the morning hours, while wheat anchors the complex. The trade has to
digest what is now a massive net combined long for the corn and soybean
complex, but will also be looking at likely continued and seasonally-declining
ratings as crops quickly dry down into harvest—hot and dry corn belt weather
is likely to add more fuel to that fire in the next ten days or so.
• Jordan issued an international tender for up to 120k tonnes of optional -origin
milling wheat, with a deadline set for tomorrow and seeking Oct shipment.
• Russian consultancy SovEcon is expecting a sharp increase in grain exports
through the Baltic states and Russian Baltic ports this month, as exports shift
away from Black Sea ports due to Ukrainian drone attacks. Baltic ports only
shipped 1 MMT of Russian grain in 2025/26 (July-June), versus 46.3 MMT
through Black Sea and Azov ports; requests for ‘26/27 shipments through the
Baltics hit 5 MMT by Aug 18, compared to 9 MMT through the Black Sea.
• Private analysts Safras & Mercado on Friday pegged the 2026/27 Brazilian
corn crop at 145.6 MMT, up slightly from 145.0 MMT previously due to increased safrinha production and ahead of 139.3 MMT in 2025/26.
• Friday afternoon’s Disaggregated CFTC Report showed managed money
funds adding a whopping 136k net corn contracts on the week ending last
Tuesday (8/25), even more than the 105k net expected by daily trade estimates; soybeans gained 49k net there, more than double the trade guess. The
rest of the complex was closer to expectations with meal +12.6k net, oil –6.1k
net, Chi wheat +12..3k net, and KC +11k net on the week to August 25.
• CBOT September Deliveries: corn 90 contracts, with next trade date available
6/29/26; meal 261 and 7/31; oil 800 and 8/19; Chi wheat 9 contracts and 6/3;
KC wheat 143 contracts and 8/27/26.

WEATHER UPDATE
• Rains were mostly confined to the northern corn belt over the weekend, with
coverage a bit lighter than expected; action will be light again this week but
again favor the northern belt, from the Dakotas into southern MN and WI.
Extended maps continue to hold rains in the western U.S., slightly drier in the
Plains and then much drier in the Midwest, up through mid-September. Temperatures will be well above-normal across the heart of the country for at least
the next week to ten days, still warm for the 11-15 day period.
• Argentine crop areas remain dry with rains holding out to fringe regions, but
Brazilian wheat will see better rains moving from south to north across the
belt this week into next—that will improve soybean area moisture as well.
FUNDAMENTAL UPDATE
Today’s chart is an update on the CBOT November soybean seasonal, including recent years and the three and five
-year averages, along with SX6 progress thus far. The most
-traded soybean contract easily posted a contract high on
Friday, the highest close for a Nov contract since late 2023,
when the SX4 contract was on its way down (it fell over
$3/bu into Aug lows). The seasonal trend for SX is a slow
chop lower from early in the growing season into harvest.
